title: Upstairs signal flow
subtitle: BH208 (audio side) and BH209 (video side): how the hall gets recorded and streamed
about: A first, good-enough map from a walkthrough on 2026-10-09. Every box and line says how sure we are. Dashed means not confirmed yet; grey with a ? means unknown. Tap anything for the details and where the information came from.

statuses.confirmed: Seen or stated plainly by the owner
statuses.tentative: Probably right: from the old diagram, a hedged answer, or an inference
statuses.unknown: We don't know yet; see the open questions

sources.old-diagram: The old splitter diagram (undated, from the 8PreX era; partly out of date)

notes.text: Two of the four hanging microphones: the center ORTF pair. Analog XLR up to BH208.
Phantom power (48V) comes from the Grace m101 preamps.
Mic make and model: unknown.
The other two hanging microphones: a wide spaced (AB) pair. Analog XLR up to BH208.
Phantom power (48V) comes from the Zoom H6.
Mic make and model: unknown.
The downstairs system at front of house (the rest of this project). There's an Ethernet link up to BH208.
The better route for the board feed would be Dante from here, but it isn't configured yet.
Today the board feed (the console's mix, L/R) comes up from the analog XLR patch bay at stage side.
All four hanging mics come into the splitter, which copies each one out to several devices at different gain ("safe" and "hot" copies, for redundancy).
Model: the owner remembers an ART S8; the old diagram says Behringer MS8000 with links 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8 on. One splitter, or two ("split twice")?
The exact outputs: see the old diagram (photo below). An updated splitter diagram is coming from the owner.
Two Grace Design m101 mic preamps for the ORTF pair, and they power it (48V).
Old diagram: their outputs went to the 8PreX inputs 1-2 and the Tio inputs 1-2 ("hot", high gain).
2026-10-09: two XLR-to-¼" cables were unplugged from the Grace outputs (probably the 8PreX legs).
The backup audio recorder (on the mic stand next to the rack). It powers the wide AB mics (48V).
Old diagram: IN 1-2 ORTF (safe), IN 3-4 AB (48V, safe), L/R board feed from Tio outputs 3-4.
The main device. One Zoom F8, 8 inputs. Its main mix goes into the Tio1608-D.
Inputs 7-8: the board feed.
Inputs 1-6: which mic copies (safe/hot) are on which: unknown.
Which Tio inputs the main mix lands on: unknown.
Old and due to be retired "soon-ish". The F8 took over as the main device.

Old diagram: IN 1-2 ORTF hot (from the Grace), 3-4 ORTF safe, 5-6 AB safe (from the splitter), 7-8 board feed (from the Tio). The same diagram also says the board feed went to 5-6, so it contradicts itself.
2026-10-09: two TRS cables unplugged from it (the owner thinks they fed the BH208 speaker).
Stage box with Dante: turns analog into network audio and back. It's the Dante Primary Leader Clock (Y001-bTio1608D).
Sends its channels 1-6 over Dante to the Yamaha 01V96 in BH209 (01V receive 1-6).
Self-routing: its own transmit 1-2 are patched to its own receive 1-2, so whatever arrives on inputs 1-2 comes back out of analog outputs 1-2.
Receive 3-8 show orange warnings in Dante Controller (subscribed to something that isn't resolving). Cause: unknown.
Analog outputs feed the older ATEM in BH209 through XLR-to-¼" adapters (fixed on 2026-10-09).
What's on inputs 1-6: unknown. Old diagram: 1-2 ORTF hot (Grace), 3-4 ORTF safe, 5-6 AB safe, 9-10 AB hot (Tio preamps). The F8 main mix now lands somewhere on it too.
The BH208 computer running Dante Controller. Its monitor is labelled BH208-SalmonAudioRec, but Dante lists a device BH209-SalmonAudioRec. Same machine, or a naming slip?
Whether it records anything over Dante: unknown.
Five Dante devices on the network on 2026-10-09: BH208-493C-or-PostProduction3, BH209-01, BH209-SalmonAudioRec, Y001-bTio1608D, Yamaha01V-MY16. Multicast bandwidth 0 bps (all unicast).
Routing is done in Dante Controller.
Gets the audio over Dante (receive 1-6 from the Tio) and sends it on to the livestream.
Dante name Yamaha01V-MY16: a Dante card in its expansion slot.
Which 01V channels and outputs, and the cable to the ATEM Mini: unknown.
Stereo 1/3-octave graphic EQ in BH209 rack 2. What it's in line with: unknown.
Audio delay set to 248.99 ms (ch 1) and 249.99 ms (ch 2): almost certainly there to line audio up with video.
Where it sits: probably around the ATEM Production Studio 4K, maybe on the feed to downstairs. Input side or output side: unknown.
The livestream switcher. Its audio comes from the 01V96.
Cameras, streaming platform and settings: not documented yet (audio first).
The older switcher that feeds the main recording system. Its audio is the analog feed from the Tio1608-D in BH208.
Which ATEM audio inputs: unknown.
From the ATEM Mini Extreme ISO.
The main (video) recording, fed by the ATEM Production Studio 4K.
Which device actually records it: unknown.

paths.name: Recorders
paths.text: The four hanging mics → splitter → Zoom F8 (main) and Zoom H6 (backup), which record on their own. The board feed joins on the F8.

paths.name: Livestream
paths.text: Into the Tio1608-D (the F8 main mix and maybe mics; which channels is open) → Tio transmit 1-6 over Dante → Yamaha 01V96 → ATEM Mini Extreme ISO → stream.

paths.name: Main recording
paths.text: Tio1608-D analog out → XLR-to-¼" adapters → tie line to BH209 → ATEM Production Studio 4K → main recording. The Rane delay may be in here.

questions.q: Zoom F8 inputs 1-6: which mic copy (ORTF/AB, safe/hot) is on each? Are 7-8 the board feed?
Tio1608-D inputs: which ones get the F8 main mix, and what is on inputs 1-6 (the six channels sent to the 01V96)?
Which Tio analog outputs feed BH209 (1-2, from the self-routing?), and which ATEM Production Studio 4K audio inputs do they land on?
Tio receive 3-8 show orange warnings in Dante Controller. What are they subscribed to, and should they be?
Rane AD22S (≈249 ms): which signal does it delay, and is it before or after the ATEM Production Studio 4K? Is it the feed to downstairs?
Rane ME60 graphic EQ: what is it in line with?
What device records the ATEM Production Studio 4K program?
01V96 to ATEM Mini Extreme ISO: which 01V outputs, which cable, which ATEM input?
Splitter: ART S8 (owner's memory) or Behringer MS8000 (old diagram)? One splitter, or two in a chain?
Dante devices: what are BH208-493C-or-PostProduction3 and BH209-01? Is BH209-SalmonAudioRec the Mac labelled BH208-SalmonAudioRec?
The bottom of the BH208 rack has another Yamaha unit that looks like a Tio. Dante shows only one Tio. Spare, powered off, or something else?
With the 8PreX retiring: where should the Grace outputs go, and what feeds the BH208 speaker now?
The make and model of the four hanging mics.

log.text: Walkthrough with photos; this first draft.
Unplugged: two TRS cables from the 8PreX (probably the BH208 speaker) and two XLR-to-¼" cables from the Grace m101 outputs.
Fixed the analog feed to BH209 with XLR-to-¼" adapters at the Tio1608-D outputs.

photos.caption: The hall from the booth window. The hanging mics are on the thin cables from the ceiling. People blurred.

BH208: Dante Controller on screen; Zoom H6 on the stand; in the rack, top to bottom: Tio1608-D, the splitter, the Zoom F8 (small screen), two Grace m101s, the red Focusrite 8PreX, and another Yamaha unit.
Dante Controller, 2026-10-09: the 01V96 receives Tio transmit 1-6; the Tio routes its own 1-2 back to itself; Tio receive 3-8 have warnings.
BH208, the audio side (rack on the right), with the window onto the hall.
BH209, the video side: the Yamaha 01V96 (left), the multiview monitors, ATEM Software Control, a camera joystick.
BH209 rack 2: multiview, Furman power, the Rane AD22S delay (≈249 ms), the ATEM Production Studio 4K, the Rane ME60 EQ.
The old splitter diagram (8PreX era). Partly out of date: the F8 replaces the 8PreX, and the board feed now comes from the stage patch bay.
